function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Java** is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language that was originally developed by James Gosling and his team at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released in 1995. It was designed with the following goals in mind:

| Goal | What it means |
|------|---------------|
| **Write once, run anywhere (WORA)** | Java programs compile to an intermediate bytecode that runs on any device that has a Java Virtual Machine (JVM). |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything is an object (except primitives), making code modular, reusable, and easier to maintain. |
| **Strongly typed** | Types are checked at compile time, reducing runtime errors. |
| **Secure** | The JVM sandbox protects against malicious code. |
| **Portable** | Java bytecode can run on any platform (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, embedded devices, etc.) without recompilation. |
| **Multithreaded** | Built‑in support for concurrent execution. |

---

### Core Components

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| **JDK (Java Development Kit)** | Full development environment: compiler (`javac`), debugger, documentation generator, and the runtime libraries. |
| **JRE (Java Runtime Environment)** | Runtime only: JVM + core libraries needed to run Java applications. |
| **JVM (Java Virtual Machine)** | Executes Java bytecode. It performs just‑in‑time (JIT) compilation to native machine code, garbage collection, and other runtime services. |
| **JVM Languages** | Java is the most common, but other languages (Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, etc.) compile to the same bytecode. |

---

### Typical Use Cases

| Domain | Why Java? |
|--------|-----------|
| **Enterprise Applications** | Robust, scalable, and secure. Widely used in banking, insurance, and logistics. |
| **Android Apps** | Android SDK uses Java (or Kotlin) as the primary language. |
| **Web Servers & Middleware** | Servlets, JSP, Spring, Hibernate, etc. |
| **Big Data** | Hadoop, Spark, Flink – many components are written in Java. |
| **Embedded Systems** | Java ME (Micro Edition) for small devices. |
| **Desktop Applications** | Swing, JavaFX for GUI apps. |

---

### Quick Example

```java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, world!");
    }
}
```

Compile & run:

```bash
javac HelloWorld.java   # compiles to HelloWorld.class (bytecode)
java HelloWorld         # runs on the JVM
```

---

### Common Misconceptions

| Misconception | Reality |
|---------------|---------|
| **Java = JavaScript** | Completely unrelated languages. |
| **Java is slow** | Modern JVMs with JIT and tiered compilation make Java competitive with native code. |
| **Java is only for desktop** | It’s everywhere: servers, mobile, cloud, IoT, etc. |

---

### Quick Reference

| Topic | Command / Code |
|-------|----------------|
| **Check Java version** | `java -version` |
| **Compile** | `javac MyClass.java` |
| **Run** | `java MyClass` |
| **Create JAR** | `jar cf myapp.jar *.class` |
| **Run JAR** | `java -jar myapp.jar` |

---

### Resources

| Resource | Link |
|----------|------|
| Official Java SE Documentation | https://docs.oracle.com/javase/ |
| Oracle JDK Downloads | https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase-downloads.html |
| OpenJDK (free, open source) | https://openjdk.org/ |
| Java Tutorials (Oracle) | https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/ |
| Java Community Process (JCP) | https://jcp.org/ |

---

**Bottom line:** Java is a versatile, mature, and widely adopted programming language that powers everything from enterprise back‑ends to Android phones, thanks to its platform‑independent bytecode, robust ecosystem, and strong community support.
